description:
## Intent

**Demand-driven umbrella** for the three post-v0.4 bets the plan names in its v0.5+ row (*"quota-mode limit scraping, floating-widget toggle, own-the-parsing"*). This ticket exists to hold their decision context so they can be split into real tickets when demand justifies scheduling — the phase row's effort estimate is literally "demand-driven". **Split into separate tickets when scheduled**; none of the three is built inside this umbrella — including the own-the-parsing spike, which runs in its own child ticket carrying section (c)'s context (ISS-035 caught the earlier Scope/In listing the spike itself, contradicting this intent and the acceptance criteria; the scope below now agrees with both).

## (a) Quota-remaining title mode via provider limit scraping

What the quota-centric market expects: prior-art research found top menubar apps are quota-centric (**CodexBar ~19.4k / ClaudeBar ~1.4k users** per the research workflow) — this is the highest-value v0.5 item per prior-art. Decision D3 already ruled: user-selectable title modes, **$ default**, picker phase-gated — quota joins the picker only in v0.5 (plan, UI: *"mode picker exposes only shipped modes ($ + burn v0.3; quota v0.5)"*). So quota mode slots into the picker T-014 built and T-020 surfaced in settings; it must not displace the $ default. The plan says nothing about HOW limits are obtained ("provider limit scraping" is the entire spec) — source, stability, and failure behavior are all open.

## (b) Floating always-on-top widget as a settings toggle

Carries the original owner ask verbatim: **"statusbar if possible xor a floating widget"**. The architecture verdict chose "Menubar over floating widget" for v1; the widget returns here as a settings toggle, not a rival product. The original "xor" phrasing suggests mutual exclusivity with the menubar item may be the intended UX — unconfirmed (open question). Lives in the Swift helper; toggle belongs to the T-020 settings surface.

## (c) Own-the-parsing spike

Checkpointed incremental extraction of `~/.claude/projects` + `~/.codex/sessions` replacing ccusage for the **full tier**. Why it matters (plan, three places):
- Measured reality: full pipeline is **60–80 s** on the owner corpus (6.5 GiB + 59 GiB) and `--since` gives **no speedup**, so "periodic authoritative full scans remain a fact of life through v0.4; checkpoints cannot reduce ccusage's scan cost. Own-the-parsing (v0.5) is the only true incremental path."
- Pricing: ccusage's price provenance is currently **authoritative**; spendbar makes "no independent repricing claims **until owned parsing (v0.5) proves token-by-model facts sufficient**" — this spike is what could lift that restriction.
- We already own part of the parsing: Codex attribution is ours because ccusage's `codex session` `directory` field is the date dir, not the cwd (verified; handover gotcha) — rollout-log head-reads with basename+regex gate + realpath containment.

A successful spike removes the periodic 60–80 s scans and enables independent pricing provenance; it also dissolves risk #2 (ccusage drift under the pin). This section is the decision context the child spike ticket carries when split — it is not a work authorization for this umbrella.

## Scope

**In:** capturing intent and decision context; when a sub-item is scheduled, creating the child ticket that carries the relevant context from this umbrella (for (c), the child is the own-the-parsing SPIKE — feasibility + differential correctness only, not the production migration) and linking it from here.
**Out:** building ANY of the three inside this umbrella — including the own-the-parsing spike itself, which previously appeared under Scope/In in contradiction with the intent (ISS-035/ISS-036); shipping any of the three without a demand signal; production replacement of ccusage (that is a follow-on ticket the spike would justify); notifications/bundle work (T-021).

## Constraints

- Own-the-parsing spike fixtures MUST be synthetic: no real transcript data or personal paths may enter fixtures — the corpus lives in the owner's home dirs and none of it may be committed.
- `usage.py` remains the frozen oracle; the existing parity/golden harness (see 2026-07-31-03 handover: 266-case parity, cases.json single registry) is the reference frame for any output-affecting change, governed by the published delta allowlist and the `--format json` pressure valve (D5).
- `package.json` never carries an author field.

## Acceptance criteria
1. When any sub-item is scheduled, it is split out as its own ticket carrying the relevant context from this umbrella, and this umbrella links to the children (this is the umbrella's only hard deliverable); no implementation or spike work is committed under this umbrella's own ID
2. Quota mode (when split): appears as an additional entry in the existing title-mode picker; $ remains the default; quota-unavailable states degrade stale-but-honest (greyed/absent, never a fabricated number)
3. Floating widget (when split): reachable as a settings toggle; always-on-top; renders from the same service snapshot as the menubar (no second data path)
4. Own-the-parsing spike (when split — executed only in its child ticket, never here): the child ticket requires a checkpointed incremental extractor over SYNTHETIC fixture corpora whose aggregates are differentially compared against a ccusage full-scan ground truth, with checkpoint-resume correctness demonstrated (kill mid-scan, resume, same totals), and a written go/no-go on whether token-by-model facts suffice for independent pricing provenance
5. No real transcript data, home paths, or personal names appear in any fixture, test, or committed artifact produced under this umbrella

## Risks
Quota scraping rests on undocumented provider surfaces — brittle, breakage-prone, and possibly ToS-sensitive; shipping it makes spendbar hostage to provider changes in exactly the way the accuracy-first positioning cannot afford. The floating widget can drift into a second product if it grows its own data path. Own-the-parsing is the largest correctness bet in the plan: it touches the parity story, the pricing provenance downgrade, and the ccusage pin all at once — a half-migrated state would be worse than either endpoint. Umbrella risk: building inside this ticket instead of splitting loses per-item review and demand gating — which is exactly why the spike is scoped OUT of this umbrella, not in.

## Open questions (owner decisions)
1. Demand gate: what signal (user requests, install counts, CodeBurn pressure) justifies scheduling each sub-item? The plan says only "demand-driven".
2. Quota scraping source: which provider surfaces expose limits (local files? APIs? app scraping?), how stable/ToS-safe are they, and what cadence — plan is entirely silent; this likely needs its own research spike before the ticket is even written.
3. Floating widget xor menubar: does enabling the widget hide the status item (the original ask's 'xor'), or can both coexist? Owner call.
4. Own-the-parsing production path: if the spike passes, does owned parsing replace ccusage outright or run as the full tier with ccusage kept as a cross-check? Affects the pin, contract tests, and risk #2.
5. Pricing source once independent: where do per-model prices come from and how is their provenance recorded, once ccusage's pricing is no longer authoritative?
6. Does the widget need the flat .app (T-021) or does it work bundle-less? Informed by T-019's spike learnings.
title: Quota mode, floating widget toggle, own-the-parsing spike
